terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with the dative
evidence: Hor. A. P. 159: (puer) gestit paribus collūdere (Lewis & Short)
Schott. Conf., Dē lūdō pilae: Collūdēmus nōnnihil?
terms.comment: To play together, to play with someone. Rare in the classical authors (Lewis & Short: “very rare”), but the ordinary word of the sixteenth-century school colloquia, like collūsor, a playmate (Cic., Plin. Ep.). In law it is also to collude. Plain ūnā lūdere, as in the example, says the same.

sources: Lewis & Short: colludo · Lewis & Short: collusor
